description: Single-panel dual-axis scatter plot, no sub-panels. The x-axis is "Phosphorus Content (wt.%)" spanning 0 to 0.05 with major ticks every 0.01. The left y-axis is "Impact Energy (J/cm²)" spanning 20 to 140 with ticks every 20; the right y-axis is "Brinell Hardness Number" spanning 280 to 360 with ticks every 10. Two series are plotted with error bars and labelled in-plot: "Impact Energy (J/cm²)" as filled circles (read on the left axis) and "Brinell Hardness" as filled squares (read on the right axis, label placed centrally). Four phosphorus levels are sampled: near 0, between 0 and 0.01, near 0.02, and between 0.04 and 0.05 wt.% P. The impact-energy circles fall progressively — the first sits just below the 140 J/cm² gridline, the last just above the 20 J/cm² gridline — with the steepest loss occurring between the two highest phosphorus contents. The hardness squares rise monotonically from near the 290 gridline to near the 340 gridline, their error bars widening at the highest phosphorus level. No numeric data labels are printed; values are only readable relative to gridlines. The two series are anti-correlated, showing that phosphorus raises aged hardness while sharply degrading Charpy V-notch impact energy.

observations.observation: The plot uses two y-axes: left 'Impact Energy (J/cm²)' with gridline ticks every 20 units from 20 to 140, and right 'Brinell Hardness Number' with ticks every 10 units from 280 to 360.
The x-axis is labelled 'Phosphorus Content (wt.%)' and spans 0 to 0.05 with major ticks at 0.01 intervals.
Impact energy is plotted as filled circles (labelled 'Impact Energy (J/cm²)' inside the panel) and Brinell hardness as filled squares (labelled 'Brinell Hardness'), both with vertical error bars.
Four phosphorus levels are sampled: one at essentially 0 wt.% P, one between 0 and 0.01, one at about 0.02, and one between 0.04 and 0.05 wt.% P.

The impact-energy values decrease monotonically with phosphorus content, the lowest-phosphorus point lying just below the 140 J/cm² gridline and the highest-phosphorus point lying just above the 20 J/cm² gridline.
The steepest loss of impact energy occurs between the points near 0.02 and between 0.04-0.05 wt.% P, where the value drops by roughly half.
Brinell hardness increases monotonically with phosphorus content, from near the 290 HB gridline at the lowest phosphorus level to near the 340 HB gridline at the highest.
The hardness error bars are largest at the highest phosphorus content, spanning approximately from the 330 to the 350 gridlines.
No numeric data labels or table values are printed on the panel; individual data values can only be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states the figure plots Charpy V-notch impact energy at room temperature and hardness versus phosphorus content in the age-hardened (10 h at 530-C) condition.
The caption states the figure shows a decrease in impact energy and increased aged hardness with increasing phosphorus content.
The citing text states that phosphorus increases the hardness of aged steels but dramatically decreases the notch toughness by more than 80%.
The citing text identifies the material as Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C steels aged for 10 h at 530-C.
The citing text links phosphorus segregation during solidification to promotion of j-carbide (κ-carbide) precipitation along austenite grain boundaries as the mechanism affecting notch toughness.

subfigures.description: One dual-axis scatter plot: phosphorus content (wt.%, x, 0-0.05) versus impact energy (J/cm², left y, 20-140, filled circles) and Brinell hardness number (right y, 280-360, filled squares), both series carrying error bars and labelled in-plot. Impact energy falls monotonically with phosphorus; hardness rises monotonically.
